items.name: Gullstjerne
items.observations: Original botanical watercolor shows Gagea lutea as a single slender spring bulbous plant with a long, broad glossy basal leaf emerging at the bulb, a thin upright stem, and an umbel of five golden six-tepalled star-shaped flowers. Tiny anthers, green styles, folded green outer tepal bands and narrow bracts are visible. The small papery bulb and fine fibrous roots communicate its early-spring geophyte habit and distinguish it from buttercups.
items.limitations: The bulb and the inflorescence are enlarged for identification at small screen sizes; plants vary in the number of yellow flowers, from two to seven, and the breadth and curvature of the basal leaf. Outer tepals and green stripes are partly obscured in the frontal view. The watercolor emphasizes golden highlights and stylizes the flower arrangement; it is not a photograph, not a calibrated specimen and not intended as the sole basis of species identification.
